newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - RESEARCH ALERT - Kimberley 'strong buy'.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - RESEARCH ALERT - Kimberley 'strong buy'.

text.p: Broker D&D Tolhurst has issued a "strong buy" recommendation for Western Australian based junior diamond explorer Kimberley Diamond Company NL.

It noted Kimberley's strategic alliance with South African mining house JCI Ltd, its significant investment in emerging Indonesian gold producer Lone Star Exploration NL, the discovery of a gem-quality diamond at its Blina prospect and a potential commercial bentonite project.

"These events provide the foundation for achieving the longer term corporate objective: establishing KDC as an international resource house - the emerging Normandy (Mining Ltd) of the nineties perhaps?", analyst Bill Kable said.
Kable said JCI's 12 percent investment in KDC this year was accompanied by statements by the companies which suggested the intent to develop a mutually rewarding relationship.
"This could lead to KDC acquiring JCI assets in Africa or KDC acquiring assets within Australasia with JCI's backing," he said.

"In either case, the incentive for JCI is to gain value for projects that otherwise would be completely undervalued by the market. The incentive for KDC is obvious, to develop into a major mining house with the backing of JCI," he said.

Kable said the Lone Star share price, which has easied from its highs earlier in the year, should rally strongly with the release this month of the resource update on the Awak Mas gold project and a commitment to develop the project thereafter.
"KDC provides potential investors in LSE with a leveraged entry into an exciting Indonesian gold play," he said.
The broker said results of final stage processing of a bulk sample from the company's Blina diamond prospect were being awaited with anticipation.
KDC reported last week it had been encouraged by the recovery of 12 diamonds weighing a total 5.35 carats at the prospect. KDC shares were steady at 23 cents at midmorning.
